analysis:
Examined the three modified ProviderLoop files. (1) ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift (head 67-97) replaces the unbounded shutdown unload loop with unloadAllModelsForShutdown(). Each slot gets a 15s bounded wait, and slots whose retirement never completes are abandoned, with a warning, until process exit. I traced the ShutdownUnloadFlag logic: for an unload owned by another task, the wait ends only when the slot is removed or the deadline passes. For our own unload, it ends when the task returns. A slot that remains resident is added to `abandoned`, so the loop terminates. This adds no new data exposure and no key or credential handling. Plaintext KV or GPU residue (T-028, TB-007) persists until process exit, which is the same as the old behavior, where shutdown could hang until --force. Availability improves (TB-003). The shutdown ordering is unchanged: coordinator.shutdown() and drainNativeMiMoOwners() still run before the unload. (2) ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head 565, 591) adds the selected-model recovery task to the shutdown cancellation set and calls the new helper. (3) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift (head 304-310) enqueues background loads of cold selected models after startup preload, using the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery, which was not supplied.

Open integration questions, none proven to be regressions: (a) The enqueue guard checks only Task.isCancelled, isShuttingDown and startupPreloadStopRequested. It does not check servingDrain.refusing, which the neighbouring updateAggregateCapacity call does check. Recovery code must itself honor the add-on hold and model-load fence (TB-012/T-059), so models are not loaded beside running VMs; I could not verify this. (b) performPreRegistrationShutdown (StartupShutdown, base 29-45) cancels only startupPreloadTask. It does not cancel selectedModelRecovery, which Serve.swift's normal shutdown does. A recovery load racing pre-registration shutdown relies on the load-install guard rejecting late slots; I could not verify this. (c) Recovery loads must use allowEviction:false and the same admission and fail-closed self-test retirement rules (failedSelfTestHashes, retiringModels). Request a review of ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift.
